spatial_entity.notes: Regional claim centered on the Samarkand/Panjikent documentary milieu. It is not projected onto the full Sogdian merchant diaspora or onto a single empire polygon.

claim.date_text_original: tenth regnal year of Tarkhun, king of Samarkand (ca. 709-710 CE)
claim.summary: A Sogdian marriage contract probably concluded at Samarkand in 709-710 CE treats becoming another person's slave as a recognized legal-status contingency, distinct from hostage, prisoner and dependent status. This supports a conservative P2 classification for early eighth-century Sogdiana. Wider evidence that Sogdian merchants traded slaves, including a 639 CE female-slave sale contract from Turfan, is retained only as contextual qualification because diaspora commerce outside Sogdiana cannot establish territorial prevalence in the homeland.

territorial_practice.notes: P2 reflects source-native legal recognition of slave status in the Samarkand documentary milieu. It does not rise to P3 from Sogdian participation in slave commerce elsewhere: the inspected evidence does not yet establish the institutional breadth, labour settings or prevalence of slavery across Sogdiana itself.

source.title: Marriage i. The Marriage Contract in the Pre-Islamic Period ii. Sogdian Marriage Contract
source.independence_notes: Modern specialist edition/translation and discussion of Mount Mugh documents Nov. 3-4, based on the Sogdian legal text and earlier editions by Livshits and others.
source.reliability_limitations: The contract recognizes slavery as a possible legal status but does not quantify slaveholding or demonstrate demographic prevalence across Sogdiana.

evidence.directness: critical translation of surviving Sogdian legal documents
evidence.locator: Nov. 3 lines 11-17; Nov. 4 lines 7-15; discussion dating the contract to ca. 709-710 CE and probably Samarkand

source.title: Sogdian Trade
source.author_or_institution: Étienne de la Vaissière; Encyclopaedia Iranica
source.independence_notes: Specialist synthesis of Sogdian commerce and documentary evidence.
source.reliability_limitations: Evidence that Sogdians traded slaves across Eurasia establishes merchant participation, not the prevalence or territorial organization of slavery inside Sogdiana.

source.title: A Sogdian sale contract of a female slave from the period of the Gaochang kingdom under the rule of Qu clan
source.author_or_institution: Yutaka Yoshida; Takao Moriyasu; Xinjiang Uighur Autonomous Museum
source.independence_notes: Dedicated edition of the Sogdian-language female-slave sale contract excavated at Astana/Turfan.
source.reliability_limitations: The transaction occurred at Turfan under Gaochang rule, outside Sogdiana; it cannot be used as territorial evidence for the Sogdian homeland merely because the contract is in Sogdian and involves Sogdians.

geometry.resolution_method: Resolve the Samarkand/Panjikent documentary context and contemporaneous Sogdian political geography separately. Do not use modern Uzbekistan/Tajikistan, a Silk Road diaspora footprint, or a maximum-extent imperial polygon as a territorial proxy.
